A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, including complete supplementary material in Appendices A–G. The text, equations, Tables 1–14 and Figures 1–10 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Ego-Exo4D and HANDAL-X evaluations, ablations, test-time training analyses and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, test-time training analyses and qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The conditional segmentation architecture, DINOv3 backbones, conditioning token, mask and visibility heads, training losses and test-time adaptation procedure are unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ego-Exo4D for Ego2Exo and Exo2Ego correspondence and HANDAL-X for cross-view generalization and fine-tuning. The activity scenarios and same-view training coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator rows in Tables 1, 2, 5 and 8 are unchanged. This includes the Ego-Exo4D baselines, HANDAL-X comparisons and XSegTx/DINOv3 control; altered citation numbers do not indicate different methods.

E3.justification: Sections 3.3 and 4.1 and Appendices B–D retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations and training budgets. Direction-specific TTT steps and adapted-layer counts are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The loss, augmentation, backbone, linear-probing, mask-prediction and TTT ablations are retained unchanged. Activity/object-size analyses, latency analysis and qualitative failure examples also match across the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No statistical uncertainty reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. Both report 44.57% Ego-Exo4D mIoU in Table 1 and identical HANDAL-X results with and without TTT in Tables 2 and 8; ablation values and plotted results also match.

T1.justification: The masked-feature definitions, token construction and Equations (1)–(5), including the loss and cosine-prediction formulas, are mathematically unchanged. Apparent equation differences in extracted text are absent from the rendered mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims concerning a simple conditional segmentation framework, cycle-consistency supervision, effective TTT and state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of object-size effects, TTT benefits and direction-dependent adaptation are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same incomplete-mask, distractor and missed-object failure patterns and proposed use of temporal cues.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix B retain the same optimizer, learning rates, image and batch sizes, EMA, hardware and runtime information. The code-access statement and link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2's general citation cluster adds PromptHub, FCL-COD and AdaMem and removes Audio-visual World Models and PlotCraft. These limited reference substitutions leave the substantive discussion of prior methods and the paper's novelty positioning unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 changes 'Dataset' to 'Datasets'; the version/date stamp and some bibliographic metadata are updated. The main prose, section order and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds blue shading to the Ours row in Table 1 and the Ours/DINOv3 row in Table 5. References reflow slightly, while figure content, table structures and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: The added highlighting in Tables 1 and 5 provides slight visual consistency, while the reference substitutions and wording correction have little effect on the argument. The scientific explanation, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged, leaving overall paper quality essentially the same.
